fixes.explanation: Paul says it right there: the gospel is what he preached to them, what they received, and what they "stand firm" in (1 Corinthians 15:1). That's a church planted like a tree. I think Paul is smiling a little as he writes it.

The word is "received." Paul says, "For what I received I passed on to you…" (1 Corinthians 15:3) Yes, he's writing this very letter, but he didn't make up the message. He got it first and then passed it on.

Yes, and the phrase shows up twice in a row. Christ died for our sins "…according to the Scriptures…" and He was raised on the third day "…according to the Scriptures…" (1 Corinthians 15:3-4) Same phrase for the death and for the raising. Count them, friend, there are two.

Paul says Christ "…appeared to Cephas and then to the Twelve." (1 Corinthians 15:5) Cephas is the name Jesus gave Simon, which is translated Peter (John 1:42). The Twelve are the disciples Jesus called to Him (Matthew 10:1). So the Twelve are next on Paul's list.

The Pharisees aren't on Paul's list here. He says Christ "…appeared to Cephas and then to the Twelve." (1 Corinthians 15:5) The Twelve are the disciples Jesus called to Him (Matthew 10:1). Paul is naming those who saw Him.

Not the chief priests. Paul says Christ "…appeared to Cephas and then to the Twelve." (1 Corinthians 15:5) The Twelve are the disciples Jesus called to Him (Matthew 10:1). That's the next name on the list.

That number isn't in this verse. Paul says Christ "…appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once…" (1 Corinthians 15:6) A hundred twenty would leave hundreds of people standing outside asking what they missed.

Paul says the opposite. He says that of the more than five hundred, "…most of whom are still living, though some have fallen asleep." (1 Corinthians 15:6) Most are still living, and only some have fallen asleep. So this one is false, friend.

Right on. Paul says the more than five hundred are "…most of whom are still living, though some have fallen asleep." (1 Corinthians 15:6) So most are still alive when he writes. Only some have fallen asleep.
